newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to meet Jordan prime minister in Jericho.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to meet Jordan prime minister in Jericho.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will meet Jordan's prime minister in Jericho West Bank self-rule enclave on Thursday to discuss troubled peace moves with Israel, PLO officials said on Wednesday.
"They are going to discuss the peace process...and the crisis over the delay in reaching an agreement on the Hebron issue," Arafat adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.
For two months, PLO and Israeli negotiators have been struggling to close a deal on implementing Israel's handover of most of the West Bank town of Hebron to the Palestinian Authority.
The deal was signed more than a year ago by the PLO and Israel's previous centre-left government.
Palestinians fear Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ousted the previous government in May elections, wants to scrap peace moves based on trading occupied Arab land for peace.
Netanyahu, who opposes trading land for peace, says he will nonetheless implement agreements signed between the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) and Israel's former government.
But Netanyahu wants to alter the Hebron accord to guarantee additional security for the 400 Jews living and studying in the city amidst more than 100,000 Palestinians.

The main sticking point between the sides has been Israel's insistence on "hot pursuit" -- the right to chase wanted persons in the 80 percent of Hebron to come under PLO-rule. The PLO refuses to make changes in the signed deal.

Israeli media said on Wednesday Israel had softened its hot pursuit demand and was ready to settle for a formulation saying the situation in Hebron, the only West Bank Palestinian town with Jewish settlers living inside it, would be like that in other West Bank towns already handed to the PLO.
Israel's Channel One Television said one consideration in the softening of Israel's stance was that Netanyahu wanted a deal in hand before he travelled to Portugal on Monday.

PLO negotiators said Israel submitted a paper on Tuesday night to them but that no progress had been made on main sticking points. They said the paper's language on hot pursuit was different from that previously used by Israel but that there was no change in the content.

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross called Arafat on Tuesady night, PLO officials said, to say that Israel's new paper reflected a more flexible stance. Ross urged Arafat to show flexibility as well.

Under an interim PLO-Israel deal, Israel was to hand over seven major West Bank towns to the PLO. It handed over six. The Hebron pullout was delayed by a wave of Moslem militant suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.
